summary: <strong>Background:</strong> Women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) who achieve clinical pregnancy following fresh in vitro fertilization (IVF)/intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) carry an elevated miscarriage risk. However, individualized risk stratification after clinical pregnancy confirmation but before outcome determination remains challenging in clinical practice. <strong>Objective:</strong> This study aimed to develop, externally and prospectively validate over time, and interpret a machine learning–based risk stratification model for women with PCOS who had achieved a confirmed clinical pregnancy after fresh IVF/ICSI. <strong>Methods:</strong> This multicenter study included 8911 clinical pregnancy IVF/ICSI cycles across development (n=7241; miscarriages: n=973), external validation (n=1170; miscarriages: n=146), and prospective temporal validation (n=500; miscarriages: n=62) cohorts. Prespecified predictors contained no observed missing values; training-fold median imputation was kept only as a leakage-safe fallback. A total of 13 candidate machine learning and traditional statistical algorithms were compared internally using repeated stratified 5-fold cross-validation (5 repeats) within the development cohort; preprocessing and hyperparameter tuning were performed exclusively in training folds. A prelocked Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model was carried forward unchanged for external and prospective temporal validation. Cross-fitted logistic recalibration of averaged XGBoost out-of-fold probabilities was evaluated as a secondary development-sample diagnostic analysis. Model performance encompassed discrimination, precision-recall, calibration, threshold-based metrics, decision curve analysis, risk stratification, and Shapley additive explanations–based interpretability. <strong>Results:</strong> Miscarriage rates were 13.4% (973/7241), 12.5% (146/1170), and 12.4% (62/500) for the development, external validation, and prospective temporal validation cohorts, respectively. In repeated cross-validation, XGBoost (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC] 0.885, 95% CI 0.874-0.896) and LightGBM (AUC 0.882, 95% CI 0.871-0.893) showed comparable discrimination; the paired XGBoost-LightGBM DeLong test was not significant (Holm-adjusted <i>P</i>=.07). Raw XGBoost out-of-fold probabilities overestimated absolute risk (mean predicted risk 30.3% vs observed risk 13.4%); cross-fitted recalibration within the development cohort improved calibration but was not propagated to validation cohorts. The locked XGBoost model achieved AUCs of 0.787 (95% CI 0.748-0.827; Brier score 0.099) in external validation and 0.763 (95% CI 0.709-0.816; Brier score 0.104) in prospective temporal validation, showing cross-cohort performance attenuation. Risk-quartile stratification using fixed development-cohort cutoffs showed consistent event enrichment across validation cohorts, but positive predictive values remained modest. Shapley additive explanations analysis identified anti-Müllerian hormone, endometrial thickness on the day of human chorionic gonadotropin administration, and basal luteinizing hormone as leading predictors. <strong>Conclusions:</strong> The locked XGBoost model using routine preoutcome variables may support miscarriage risk stratification and counseling for women with PCOS with clinical pregnancy after fresh IVF/ICSI. Given cross-cohort discrimination loss and calibration drift, it should serve only as a risk-ranking tool, not for diagnosis or treatment selection. Local calibration monitoring is mandatory before any real-world clinical deployment.
title: Miscarriage Risk Prediction for Women With Polycystic Ovary Syndrome Who Achieve Clinical Pregnancy After Fresh Embryo Transfer: Multicenter Development, Geographic External Validation, and Prospective Temporal Validation Study

summary: Background: Advances in the diagnosis and treatment of childhood cancer have substantially improved survival, resulting in a growing population of survivors of childhood cancer who may experience long-term treatment-related sequelae. Cognitive late effects are an important long-term consequence of childhood cancer and can affect cognitive functioning, psychosocial well-being, and quality of life. Digital health interventions offer accessible and flexible approaches to managing cognitive difficulties among children with cancer. However, the existing evidence has not yet been comprehensively synthesized. Objective: This study aimed to map and synthesize the existing evidence on digital health interventions for cognitive management among children with cancer; characterize intervention modalities, delivery approaches, and functional components; and identify evidence gaps and priorities for future research. Methods: This scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Arksey and O’Malley framework and the PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews) checklist. Six academic databases, including PubMed, Embase (Ovid), CINAHL, PsycINFO, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library, were systematically searched for relevant studies published between January 2010 and August 2026. Eligibility criteria were developed using the population-concept-context framework. Two reviewers independently performed study screening and data extraction. The methodological quality of included studies was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Screening was performed independently at the title/abstract and full-text stages, with disagreements resolved through discussion and, when necessary, consultation with a third reviewer. Descriptive statistics and thematic content analysis were used to synthesize the findings. Results: A total of 5371 records were identified through the literature search. Following screening, 19 publications representing 14 independent study samples and involving 566 children with cancer were included. Four digital health modalities were identified: computer-based interventions, internet-based interventions, mobile apps, and neurofeedback training. Computer-based interventions were the predominant modality. Across these modalities, working memory and attention were the most frequently targeted cognitive domains, while feasibility, acceptability, and adherence were the most commonly assessed implementation-related outcomes. However, relatively few interventions incorporated coach support, telephone-based communication, or educational components, and none evaluated economic outcomes. Conclusions: Although digital health interventions show promise for supporting cognitive function in children with cancer, substantial gaps remain in the current evidence. This scoping review mapped the field according to intervention modalities, delivery approaches, and functional components, rather than focusing solely on the efficacy of individual technologies. Future research should prioritize the development of multidimensional, personalized, and functionally integrated digital health interventions that combine cognitive training with supportive care, education, monitoring, and communication. Multicenter randomized controlled trials should subsequently evaluate these interventions using clinically meaningful outcomes, with comprehensive assessments of safety, adherence, implementation, and health economic outcomes to establish their effectiveness, feasibility, and sustainability.
title: Application of Digital Health Interventions for Cognitive Management in Children With Cancer: Scoping Review

summary: Background: Frontline health workers in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) often face barriers that compromise care quality, including limited training, high patient loads, inadequate access to updated clinical guidance, and resource constraints. Working in underserved settings further exacerbates challenges to providing accurate, complete, and empathetic responses. Addressing these gaps requires innovative tools to support FLWs in real time. Objective: This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of ChatGPT-3.5 (OpenAI) in enhancing the quality of FLWs’ responses to health inquiries in Lagos, Nigeria. Methods: In this observational study, 36 licensed frontline health workers (doctors, nurses, and community health workers) practicing general or primary care in Lagos, Nigeria, generated responses to 15 patient-generated health questions covering maternal and neonatal health, family planning, and sexually transmitted infections. Each FLW produced responses using their own knowledge and available resources (human-only) and with ChatGPT-3.5 assistance (GPT-aided). A panel of 4 clinicians evaluated responses using a 5-point Likert scale for accuracy, empathy, contextualization, completeness, safety, and overall preference. In addition, 8 nonclinician health seekers assessed a subset of responses across 3 themes: Caring, Trust, and Ease of Understanding. Results: Across 1080 responses from 36 frontline health workers, GPT-aided responses significantly outperformed human-only responses on all clinician-rated metrics (<.001), with the largest gains observed in completeness, empathy, and overall preference, particularly among community health extension workers (CHEWs). Nonclinician evaluators also favored GPT-aided responses across all themes, with a strong preference for trust. Conclusions: This study provides empirical evidence that a large language model (ChatGPT-3.5) enhances the completeness, empathy, and perceived trust of responses by frontline health workers in Lagos, Nigeria. These findings underscore the potential of integrating ChatGPT-3.5 to strengthen health care delivery in resource-limited settings, highlighting the necessity for capacity building and further investigation into its safe, equitable, and effective implementation.
title: Evaluating Frontline Health Workers’ Responses to Patient Inquiries With and Without Large Language Model Support in Nigeria: Observational Study

summary: <strong>Background:</strong> Clinical communication skills are a core yet complex competency in medical education and practice. However, early-stage medical students often struggle to apply communication frameworks in practice due to limited opportunities for structured simulation training. Generative AI (GenAI)–supported training has the potential to offer a scalable and innovative approach for clinical communication skills training. <strong>Objective:</strong> This study examined the longitudinal development of medical students’ clinical communication skills over 1 academic year and investigated whether AI-powered simulation contributed to differential improvement relative to conventional training. In addition, the study explored motivational, behavioral, and affective mechanisms associated with communication skills development. <strong>Methods:</strong> A nonblinded randomized controlled design was used at a medical school in the United Kingdom, with students assigned either to the control group (n=28, 56%) or to the AI group (n=22, 44%), who practiced with SimPatient, a patient-simulator chatbot accessed through a web browser. Communication skills performance was assessed using standardized objective structured clinical examinations (OSCE) scores relative to the pass marks to enable comparison across time points. Paired <i>t</i> tests and difference-in-differences (DID) analyses were conducted between groups and over time to examine changes in communication skills. Latent change score modeling was used to identify predictors of communication skills change. Sentiment analysis was conducted on 6120 comments from AI-student conversations. Finally, a system quality survey was used to assess participants’ feedback on the AI-powered simulator. <strong>Results:</strong> Latent change score modeling showed that gains in intrinsic motivation and behavioral learning were significant predictors of students’ communication skills change. The AI group showed a greater descriptive increase in communication skills than the control group, yet the between-group difference was not statistically significant. Within the AI group, consultations whose lexical tone trended more strongly toward resolution (consultation tone) were descriptively associated with communication skills improvement; given the small subsample (n=17), this finding is reported as exploratory. The AI group’s confidence level in AI use was negatively associated with communication skills improvement, while the group nevertheless reported a generally high level of satisfaction with the system. <strong>Conclusions:</strong> In this study, medical students’ clinical communication skills increased over the academic year, with this development most strongly associated with their motivation and behavioral engagement; the AI-supported group did not differ significantly from conventional training. The simulator responded appropriately and provided a usable environment for practicing foundational communication behaviors but was limited in capturing the affective complexity, vulnerability, and narrative unpredictability of real clinical encounters. In conclusion, this study suggests that GenAI holds promise for supporting foundational clinical communication training and providing positive practice environments, thereby fostering motivation and behavioral engagement.
title: Evaluating an AI-Powered Patient Simulator for Communication Skills Training: One-Year Randomized Controlled Trial

summary: Background: Large language models (LLMs) show great potential for widespread application in the field of nursing; however, their limitations include hallucinations, insufficient domain knowledge, and delays in updating evidence. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), by combining external knowledge retrieval with text generation, holds promise for optimizing model outputs. However, current evidence on the use of RAG in nursing remains fragmented and has not been systematically synthesized. Objective: This scoping review aims to map the applications of RAG in the nursing field, identify current research characteristics and gaps, and provide a foundational evidence base to inform future research and development of intelligent tools for nursing practice. Methods: This study adopted the Arksey and O’Malley scoping review framework and followed PRISMA-ScR (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses Extension for Scoping Reviews) reporting standards. We systematically searched 9 databases—PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, Cochrane Library, Scopus, CNKI, VIP Database, Wanfang Database, and Sinomed—from inception to September 2026. Backward and forward citation searches were also conducted to identify additional eligible studies. Eligible publications were restricted to those in English or Chinese during study selection. Two independent reviewers completed study screening and data extraction, and descriptive synthesis was performed for all eligible records. Results: A total of 28 studies published between 2024 and 2026 were included. The application of RAG in nursing primarily focused on 4 scenarios: patient education (n=9), nursing informatics (n=8), clinical decision support (n=7), and nursing education (n=4). The base LLMs included the GPT series, LLaMA, ChatGLM, and Doubao, among others, while the knowledge bases primarily integrated literature, clinical guidelines, institutional resources, and clinical data. Most studies relied on dense retrieval, while some incorporated hybrid retrieval, knowledge graphs, and reranking to achieve optimization. Generation and task-output evaluations were reported in 27 studies, whereas retrieval evaluation, safety and reliability evaluations, and implementation or outcome evaluations were less frequently reported. Only 4 studies were conducted in real-world clinical settings. Overall, RAG demonstrated potential to improve the accuracy and reliability of LLM-generated outputs in specific nursing tasks; however, most studies validated only in simulated environments. Conclusions: This review systematically maps and synthesizes the application scenarios, technical characteristics, reporting completeness, evaluation methods, and research outcomes of RAG from the perspective of nursing tasks, further refining the evidence landscape for RAG research in nursing contexts. By summarizing the selection of base LLMs, knowledge bases and retrieval processes, the key elements of technical reports, and the areas for tiered evaluation, this review provides evidence-informed considerations for the design, validation, and reporting of future RAG-based nursing AI systems. The findings may assist clinical nurses, nursing educators, and hospital IT teams in identifying application scenarios, key safety requirements, and evaluation priorities, while also highlighting the necessity of conducting prospective validation within real-world nursing workflows.
title: Applications, Technical Characteristics, and Evaluation Approaches of Retrieval-Augmented Generation in Nursing: Scoping Review

summary: Background: Online peer-support communities have become an increasingly important source of mental health information and support, particularly for individuals experiencing depression and anxiety. Platforms such as Reddit provide anonymous, accessible spaces where users can seek advice, share experiences, and receive community feedback. While these communities may help reduce barriers associated with stigma and access to care, concerns remain regarding the reliability, safety, and clinical appropriateness of peer-generated advice. Despite their widespread use, little empirical evidence exists regarding the extent to which highly endorsed online advice reflects evidence-based clinical recommendations. Objective: This study aimed to evaluate the extent to which highly endorsed peer advice shared on Reddit’s r/mentalhealth subreddit for depression and anxiety aligns with established national and international evidence-based clinical practice guidelines. Methods: A cross-sectional qualitative content analysis was conducted using 1065 publicly available posts from Reddit’s r/mentalhealth community related to depression and/or anxiety together with their highest-ranked responses. Posts were classified into action-based and nonaction-based advice using a large language model followed by manual verification. Action-based advice was analyzed thematically and mapped against recommendations from established, recognized national and international clinical guidelines, including the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE), the World Health Organization Mental Health Gap Action Programme (WHO mhGAP), and Australian evidence-based mental health frameworks. Thematic findings were evaluated to determine the degree of alignment with guideline recommendations. Results: Of the included posts, 327 anxiety-related and 243 depression-related discussions contained action-based advice suitable for analysis. Six overarching themes emerged: (1) seeking professional help, (2) behavioral and lifestyle changes, (3) emotional regulation and cognitive strategies, (4) interpersonal and social dynamics, (5) self-prioritization and life direction, and (6) crisis and immediate safety. Seeking professional help was the most frequently endorsed recommendation across both depression and anxiety conditions. Overall, highly endorsed advice demonstrated substantial alignment with evidence-based clinical guidance, particularly regarding professional help-seeking, behavioral activation, healthy lifestyle practices, emotional regulation, and social support. Areas of partial or limited alignment were observed primarily in discussions involving complex interpersonal circumstances, self-management beyond current evidence, and crisis situations where advice occasionally lacked the specificity or urgency recommended by clinical guidelines. Conclusions: Highly endorsed mental health advice contained within top-ranked Reddit comments generally reflects established evidence-based recommendations for managing depression and anxiety, suggesting that online peer-support forums may serve as valuable complementary sources of guidance and encouragement. Nevertheless, reliance on community-generated advice alone may be insufficient in complex or high-risk situations where professional assessment and intervention are essential. These findings provide empirical evidence supporting the potential role of moderated online peer-support communities within the broader mental health ecosystem while highlighting the importance of continued evaluation of the quality and safety of digital peer-to-peer health information.
title: Evidence-Based Alignment of Reddit Peer Advice for Depression and Anxiety: Qualitative Content Analysis

summary: Background: Postoperative mortality remains a key indicator of surgical safety and quality. Traditional risk models based on static preoperative or intraoperative variables often fail to capture dynamic physiological changes during surgery and generalize poorly across surgical types. To address these limitations, we developed and validated a deep learning framework capable of learning heterogeneous temporal patterns from intraoperative signals while maintaining interpretability and adaptability. Objective: This study aimed to develop a mixture-of-experts–based model (Postoperative Risk Modeling Expert network, PRIME-MoE) to provide dynamic, surgery-adaptive postoperative in-hospital mortality risk prediction. The primary objective was to improve prediction accuracy, cross-database robustness, and interpretability across heterogeneous surgical populations and institutions. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 173,990 surgical cases from the INSPIRE (Informative Surgical Patient Dataset for Innovative Research Environment) and HUAXI databases. PRIME-MoE used 4 one-layer unidirectional long short-term memory experts with dense softmax routing based on static surgical context. We evaluated discrimination, calibration, threshold-specific operating points, parameter count, graphics processing unit inference latency, routing patterns, and a sensitivity analysis that truncated the final 30 minutes of each operation without retraining. Results: PRIME-MoE achieved internal-test area under the receiver operating characteristic curves (AUROCs) of 93.8 (95% CI 92.3‐96.0) in INSPIRE and 90.7 (95% CI 87.1‐94.8) in HUAXI. Reciprocal evaluation retained discrimination (AUROCs 90.8 and 87.8) but showed imperfect calibration (Brier scores 0.035‐0.049; calibration slopes 0.28‐0.49), supporting site-specific recalibration. Graphics processing unit inference required a median of 11.4 ms (9.1-18.0; 3.3-45.3) per case. Without retraining, scoring 30 minutes before the recorded end of surgery retained AUROCs of 93.1 in INSPIRE and 90.2 in HUAXI. Conclusions: PRIME-MoE provides an interpretable framework for postoperative in-hospital mortality prediction and retained discrimination in reciprocal evaluation across 2 heterogeneous perioperative databases. The 30-minute analysis supports near-end-of-surgery scoring, but calibration was insufficient for direct deployment. Prospective validation, local recalibration, threshold selection, and workflow evaluation are required before clinical use.
title: Development and Validation of a Mixture-of-Experts–Based Model for Postoperative In-Hospital Mortality Risk Assessment: Multicenter Retrospective Study

summary: <strong>Background:</strong> Pediatric care resources are limited and unevenly distributed in many health systems. Caregivers increasingly turn to large language models (LLMs) for children’s health information, but real-world evidence on LLM use and response quality in general pediatric care is limited. <strong>Objective:</strong> This study aimed to characterize real-world use, consultation needs, and response quality of Xiaoyi, an LLM-based pediatric health assistant, and to evaluate the impact of expert-guided optimization on response quality. <strong>Methods:</strong> This study collected all consultation sessions submitted between April 7 and December 31, 2025, to Xiaoyi, a pediatric health assistant co-developed by Children’s Hospital of Chongqing Medical University and Zuoyi Tech. Temporal patterns of consultation activity were characterized; all sessions were annotated for pediatric subspecialty, reason for consultation, and presenting symptoms through LLM-assisted labeling with pediatrician validation. A multidisciplinary panel of 40 pediatricians evaluated Xiaoyi’s response quality over 2 rounds using predefined criteria established by expert consensus: an initial evaluation informed system optimization (prompt revision, knowledge-base and tool expansion, and validation rules) and a follow-up evaluation assessed its impact. In each round, 1000 sessions randomly sampled from the corresponding pre- or postoptimization period (2000 in total) were rated at the session level (overall quality and clinical appropriateness) and the turn level (6 predefined deficiency categories). Categorical ratings were compared using the chi-square test, and turn-level deficiency rates were compared using generalized estimating equations to account for within-session correlation. <strong>Results:</strong> Caregivers of 8266 children (median age 4.2, IQR 1.3-8 years; 4705/8266, 56.9% male) from 31 of 34 provincial-level divisions in China initiated 16,074 sessions, of which 7046 (43.8%) occurred outside routine clinic hours (08:00-17:30). Queries spanned 31 subspecialties, most frequently child health care (2025/16,074, 12.6%), pulmonology (1903/16,074, 11.8%), and gastroenterology (1833/16,074, 11.4%). The leading reasons for consultation were symptom consultation (7845/16,074, 48.8%), medical report interpretation (2531/16,074, 15.7%), and triage guidance (2515/16,074, 15.6%); among symptom consultation sessions, fever (2719/16,074, 34.7%) and cough (2349/16,074, 29.9%) were most common. After expert-guided optimization, the number of sessions rated good (n=1000) in overall quality (the response fully resolving the caregiver’s question with actionable information) increased from 652 (65.2%) to 743 (74.3%), and the number rated clinically appropriate increased from 614 (61.4%) to 874 (87.4%, both <i>P</i><.001). The turn-level deficiency rate declined from 19.4% (790/4073 turns) to 6.9% (236/3419 turns; odds ratio 0.30, 95% CI 0.24-0.37; <i>P</i><.001), with suboptimal clinical recommendations (not optimally tailored to the child’s age or clinical context) remaining the most frequent category. <strong>Conclusions:</strong> This real-world study suggests that an LLM-based health consultation assistant may complement existing pediatric care, with expert-guided optimization substantially improving response quality. However, the persistence of deficiencies highlights the need for continued monitoring and refinement to ensure clinical reliability. <strong>Trial Registration:</strong>
title: Real-World Use and Expert-Guided Optimization of a Large Language Model–Based Pediatric Health Assistant: Retrospective Observational Study

summary: This is a correction of "Unveiling Patient-Level Harms and At-Risk Clinical Groups During Hospital Cyberattacks: Systematic Review of Global Case Studies and Social Media Data".
title: Correction: Unveiling Patient-Level Harms and At-Risk Clinical Groups During Hospital Cyberattacks: Systematic Review of Global Case Studies and Social Media Data

summary: Background: Digital decision-support tools, such as the Stroke Triage App (STA), may enhance prehospital triage and clinical decision-making for suspected patients with stroke. However, implementation of decision-support tools and their impact on clinical practice remains insufficiently studied. Objective: This study aimed to investigate paramedics’ experiences with the implementation of the STA in prehospital practice by evaluating the implementation process, the implementation outcomes, and its impact on clinical workflows, while considering contextual factors that may have influenced these dimensions. Methods: STA implementation was evaluated among paramedics in 2 emergency medical services regions in the Netherlands using a sequential mixed methods approach. Actual usage data were extracted from the STA dashboard. Usability, perceived impact, and contextual factors were explored using an online survey and semistructured interviews. Results: Monthly triages ranged from 52 to 153 (median 120, IQR 107‐131). Paramedics’ individual STA use ranged from 1 to 47 times (median 7, IQR 3‐13). Out of 246 paramedics with an account, 76 (31%) completed the survey, and 9 (4%) participated in semistructured interviews. The STA was generally well accepted, supporting structured neurological assessment and communication. Swift technical support, frequent promotion, and use of local ambassadors facilitated STA use. Clinical urgency, poor workflow integration, and limited perceived added value hampered STA use. Users recommended improvements in mobile interface, login features, and additional explanation with triage advice. Conclusions: This study demonstrates that the STA achieved substantial reach and initial adoption within the prehospital setting. However, widespread acceptance did not consistently translate into routine integration in daily practice. Successful implementation depends as much on addressing organizational and human factors as on technical performance.
title: Implementation and Evaluation of the Stroke Triage App Among Paramedics in Prehospital Emergency Care: Sequential Mixed Methods Study
